title: Staggered sprint tiles and gated onramp for private instances
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a quarterly roadmap artifact: a staggered 'sprint tiles' plan that sequences gated activation lanes for Private/VPC/on‑prem customers. The goal is to provide a predictable, testable onramp that ties to OKR initiative 'Private Instance Activation' and reduces blast radius while enabling paid customer onboarding at scale.

What we are building:
- A repeatable quarter-level cadence (4 sprint tiles) where each tile is a gated experiment lane: pilot cohort -> expanded cohort -> regional scaling -> customer onboarding runway.
- Acceptance gates per tile (compatibility tests, audit log maturity, KMS integration smoke tests, performance SLO check, security signoff).
- A lightweight control plane checklist and playbook for Solutions/SEs to run activation with built-in rollback steps.
- Integration hooks for Console: cohort status, rollout stage, and per-tenant metrics surfaced in the Console Runbooks dashboard.

Why now / context:
- We’ve seen repeated churn across ad-hoc private activations; customers report unclear expectations for staging and upgrade windows. This cadence directly aligns with Q2 commercial targets and an OKR to increase private instance throughput by 3x while keeping time-to-onboard under 10 days for Lighthouse customers.

Progress and decisions so far:
- Product approved the four-tile cadence model (decision 2026-02-12).
- Security committed to expedited review for the activation checklist; preliminary KMS/HSM gating defined (security owners: Priya Shah).
- Engineering scoped a compatibility verifier microservice (ENG-3412) to run pre-activation checks; ETA for smoke APIs is 2026-03-22.
- Design provided templates for the Console cohort UI and tooltips (Figma link in artifacts).

Key artifacts and links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-onramp/PRD-staggered-tiles (draft)
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Private-Onramp-Console-Widgets
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-onramp/pulls (tracking PRs)
- Runbook draft: drive.redwood.ai/PrivateActivation-Runbook-v0.3
- Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/PrivateOnramp/activation-lanes

Acceptance criteria / exit criteria for each tile:
- Compatibility: verifier returns <1% blocked dependencies for cohort (breakdown by OS, network topology, quantized model variants).
- Security: successful KMS key rotation test, audit log ingestion at 100% (no dropped events), SAML SSO smoke test.
- Performance: 99th percentile p99 tail latency within committed SLA for reserved capacity tier during 24h soak.
- Operational: on-call runbook rehearsed with SE for at least one lighthouse tenant; rollback tested and timed <30m.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Sprint tile A (pilot): 1–2 lighthouse customers, manual activation guided by SEs, gather failure modes (2 sprints).
2) Sprint tile B (scale to cohort): automated verifier gating, first automated feature flags, increase to 10 customers in controlled regions.
3) Sprint tile C (regional expand): add cross-region compatibility checks, capacity hedging, start Dedicated integration tests.
4) Sprint tile D (onboarding runway): enable self-serve activation for qualifying customers, tie billing and SLA activation hooks.

Monitoring and regression strategy:
- Instrument per-tenant metrics (latency, error-rate, activation duration) and map to OKR dashboards weekly.
- Set regression alerts for signal drift in model-quality vs baseline prompt sets (linked to Optimize alerts).
- Maintain a rolling list of blocked dependencies and their remediation owners.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Compatibility surface area (customer infra diversity) is larger than expected. Mitigation: keep first two tiles tightly scoped to specific OS/container configs; expand matrix iteratively.
- Risk: Security gating introduces activation friction. Mitigation: parallelize security checklist automation and add a temporary fast-path for vetted lighthouse accounts with manual audit.
- Risk: Console instrumentation lag obscures real-time decisions. Mitigation: require immediate logging path with fallback batch export for first two tiles.

Follow-up tasks / next steps (owners assigned):
- ENG: deliver compatibility verifier MVP and public API (owner: Lina Gomez, ENG-5198) — target 2026-03-22.
- SECOPS: finalize KMS gating checklist and run two rehearsals (owner: Priya Shah) — target 2026-03-18.
- DX/Design: finalize Console cohort UI and tooltips; handoff to Frontend (owner: Marcus Li) — target 2026-03-08.
- PM: finalize PRD and stakeholder signoff; schedule kickoff with Sales/SE (owner: Diego Patel) — target 2026-03-12.

Open questions for cross-functional review:
- What minimum telemetry retention is required for legal/compliance vs operational debugging? (input: Legal & Security)
- Should we bundle an optional migration-assist service in the initial paid offering? (input: Revenue and Solutions)
- Are there any non-negotiable latency SLOs for private onprem customers vs hosted API? (input: SRE)

Notes for future quarters:
- If the cadence proves effective, convert tiles into an automated pipeline with a self-serve 'compatibility verifier' and one-click enrollment.
- Consider a dedicated quota/commit product for customers that want guaranteed private capacity tied to shorter activation windows.

Comments log (highlights):

- 2026-03-01 Priya: 'Security will sign off on automation if we include replayable audit proofs in the verification step.'

This ticket should be referenced in quarter planning artifacts and linked to OKR:OKR-Private-Activation-2026. It will be used as the canonical execution playbook for the quarter and a template for subsequent quarters.
